import random
import math

def generate():

    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Select unit system and define constants
    # -----------------------------
    unit_systems = ['si', 'uscs']
    unit_sel = random.randint(0, 1) # 0 for SI, 1 for USCS

    units = {
        "si": {
            "pressure": "kPa",
            "temperature": "K",
            "specific_enthalpy": "kJ/kg",
            "Cp": 1.005,  # kJ/(kg*K)
            "k": 1.4      # ratio of specific heats
        },
        "uscs": {
            "pressure": "psi",
            "temperature": "R",
            "specific_enthalpy": "Btu/lb",
            "Cp": 0.24,   # Btu/(lb*R)
            "k": 1.4      # ratio of specific heats
        }
    }

    selected_system = units[unit_systems[unit_sel]]

    unitsPressure = selected_system["pressure"]
    unitsTemperature = selected_system["temperature"]
    unitsSpecificEnthalpy = selected_system["specific_enthalpy"]
    Cp_air = selected_system["Cp"]
    k_air = selected_system["k"]

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Generate random parameters
    # -----------------------------
    if unit_systems[unit_sel] == 'si':
        Pressure1S = random.randint(90, 110)    # kPa
        T1 = random.randint(280, 300)           # K
        pr = random.randint(8, 15)              # Pressure ratio
        T3 = random.randint(1200, 1500)         # K
    else: # uscs
        Pressure1S = random.randint(12, 16)     # psi
        T1 = random.randint(500, 540)           # R
        pr = random.randint(8, 15)              # Pressure ratio
        T3 = random.randint(2100, 2700)         # R

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Perform calculations (assuming ideal Brayton cycle components)
    # -----------------------------
    # Isentropic compression (State 1 to State 2s)
    T2s = T1 * (pr)**((k_air - 1) / k_air)
    Wc = Cp_air * (T2s - T1) # Specific work input for compressor (magnitude)

    # Isentropic expansion (State 3 to State 4s)
    T4s = T3 / (pr)**((k_air - 1) / k_air)
    Wt = Cp_air * (T3 - T4s) # Specific work output from turbine (magnitude)

    # Heat input in the combustor (State 2s to State 3)
    Qin = Cp_air * (T3 - T2s)

    # Net work output of the cycle
    Work = Wt - Wc

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Format output
    # -----------------------------
    data = {
        "params": {
            "Pressure1S": Pressure1S,
            "T1": T1,
            "pr": pr,
            "T3": T3,
            "unitsPressure": unitsPressure,
            "unitsTemperature": unitsTemperature,
            "unitsSpecificEnthalpy": unitsSpecificEnthalpy,
            "Cp_air": Cp_air, 
            "k_air": k_air   
        },
        "correct_answers": {
            "Work": Work,
            "Qin": Qin
        },
        "nDigits": 3,
        "sigfigs": 3
    }

    return data

Step 1: Identify Known Values and Cycle Assumptions

We are given the following values for an Ericsson cycle:

  • Compressor inlet pressure: $P_1 = \{\{params.Pressure1S\}\} \\ \text{\{\{params.unitsPressure\}\}$
  • Compressor inlet temperature: $T_1 = \{\{params.T1\}\} \\ \text{\{\{params.unitsTemperature\}\}$
  • Pressure ratio: $r_p = \{\{params.pr\}\}$
  • Maximum temperature (Turbine inlet): $T_3 = \{\{params.T3\}\} \\ \text{\{\{params.unitsTemperature\}\}$
Assume air behaves as an ideal gas with a specific gas constant $R = \{\{params.R_air\}\} \\ \text{\{\{params.unitsGasConstant\}\}$ and that the cycle is ideal with regeneration.

Step 2: Determine State Properties for Isothermal and Isobaric Processes

In an ideal Ericsson cycle with regeneration:

  • Processes 1-2 (compression) and 3-4 (expansion) are isothermal.
  • Processes 2-3 (heat addition) and 4-1 (heat rejection) are isobaric.
Thus, the temperatures for the isothermal processes are:$$T_2 = T_1 = \{\{params.T1\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsTemperature\}\}$$ $$T_4 = T_3 = \{\{params.T3\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsTemperature\}\}$$The pressures are:$$P_2 = r_p P_1 = \{\{params.pr\}\} \times \{\{params.Pressure1S\}\} = \{\{correct_answers.Pressure2\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsPressure\}\}$$ $$P_3 = P_2 = \{\{correct_answers.Pressure2\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsPressure\}\}$$ $$P_4 = P_1 = \{\{params.Pressure1S\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsPressure\}\}$$

Step 3: Calculate Net Work Output ($W_{output}$)

For an ideal Ericsson cycle with regeneration, the net work output per unit mass is given by:$$w_{output} = R (T_H - T_L) \ln(r_p)$$where $T_H = T_3$ (high temperature reservoir), $T_L = T_1$ (low temperature reservoir), and $r_p$ is the pressure ratio.

Substitute the known values:

$$w_{output} = \{\{params.R_air\}\} \times ( \{\{params.T3\}\} - \{\{params.T1\}\} ) \times \ln( \{\{params.pr\}\} )$$

Step 4: Calculate Heat Input ($Q_{in}$)

For an ideal Ericsson cycle with regeneration, the heat input per unit mass ($q_{in}$) is supplied externally only during the isothermal expansion process (3-4). The heat exchanged during the isobaric processes (2-3 and 4-1) is handled by the regenerator.$$\q_{in} = R T_H \ln(r_p)$$where $T_H = T_3$.

Substitute the known values:

$$q_{in} = \{\{params.R_air\}\} \times \{\{params.T3\}\} \times \ln( \{\{params.pr\}\} )$$

Step 5: Final Answers

The calculated work output and heat input are:

$$W_{output} = \{\{correct_answers.Work\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsSpecificEnthalpy\}\}$$ $$Q_{in} = \{\{correct_answers.Qin\}\} \text{\{\{params.unitsSpecificEnthalpy\}\}$$
